_comment: What the race mode says in Assetto Corsa: its messages and the result card. Each key race.<name> reaches the mode
as <NAME> in capitals, dots as underscores (race.result.win is RESULT_WIN); the mode says its first line. {name}
is a placeholder the mode fills, its name letters and digits only. \n breaks the line. The placeholders:
race.result.bracket and race.result.bracket.broke_out: {et} the player's quarter-mile time, {dial} their dial-in.
race.tune.passes.one and .other: {passes} the passes run. race.tune.best: {et} the best pass's time, {speed} its speed in its unit ({mph} the bare mph, for older translations).
race.tune.stage, race.slip.pass and race.slip.pass.red_light: {pass} the pass, {passes} how many the strip allows.
race.slip.eighth.speed and race.slip.quarter.speed: {unit} the speed's unit, in capitals (MPH).
race.slip.back: {seconds} the seconds until the car goes back to the line. race.tree.dial_in: {dial} the dial-in.
race.ta.* (a time attack): {laps} the timed laps, {lap} the lap, {time} and {best} lap times as 1:23.456, {driver}
the rival's name, {rival} the rival's best lap. A format of a mod's own says its own race.<key> words the same way.
race.cops.trap.rival: {driver} the rival's name (race.your_rival when the mode has none).
A race with a field of rivals: race.place.st, .nd, .rd and .th are a place, {n} its number (1ST, 2ND, 3RD, 4TH; the
mode picks by the English endings, so a language with one form gives all four the same words). race.result.place:
{place} one of those, {count} how many raced. race.stagger.wait: {seconds} until the player may go.
race.road.hud.gap: {seconds} the gap. race.ta.wait.field: {count} the rivals still running.
